rationale: Fernwell is a small-batch botanical skincare label. The direction leans on a living green anchored by warm paper neutrals so product photography reads as fresh rather than clinical. Type pairs a humanist serif for headings with a quiet grotesque body to feel crafted, not corporate. Every choice defers to the plant material: the brand is the frame, never the subject.

palette.semantic: Deep fern green — the brand anchor; used for logo, primary buttons, and dominant surfaces.
Sage — a softer supporting green for section backgrounds and secondary chrome.
Marigold — a warm counterpoint that draws the eye to a single call to action per view.
Warm paper — the default canvas; keeps product imagery feeling natural and unlit.
Near-black pine — high-contrast body text on the paper background.
Dried-stem grey — captions, metadata, and disabled states.

typography.semantic: A humanist serif with soft optical sizing — reads crafted and editorial, echoing apothecary labels.
A neutral grotesque that stays quiet under the serif and keeps long ingredient copy readable.
Small-caps captioning for botanical names and provenance notes.

layout.semantic: Full-bleed product photograph on one side, generous text column on the other — lets the plant material carry the page.

cohesion.summary: Tightly cohesive: a single green family carries every surface and the paper neutral unifies imagery. The marigold accent is the only high-chroma note, so it never competes with itself.

principles.title: Plant first, brand second
principles.detail: Botanical material is always the visual subject; brand chrome frames it and never overlaps it.

principles.title: One warm note per view
principles.detail: The marigold accent appears exactly once on a screen — a single call to action — so it always means the same thing.

principles.title: Paper, never white
principles.detail: Backgrounds use the warm paper neutral, never pure #ffffff, so photography reads as natural light rather than studio strobe.
